title: Zero hold-power
statement: Holding the written or expelled or circulating state costs zero continuous power. Energy is spent only on write/erase or on the incident drive.
notes: Shared by latches persistent currents superflow and the mirror extra-power row.

title: Connected spatial buffer
statement: The machine needs a connected responding volume at least of order its screening or coherence length. Below that the collective output collapses.
value_text: order of the screening / coherence / wall length
notes: Class not a single number. Screening ~10–20 nm; London λ ~40–50 nm; domain wall few–tens of nm.

title: Thermal cliff
statement: A critical temperature destroys the ordered or coherent or crystalline population that the machine uses.
notes: Same kind of demand not the same number. Attach per design; do not equate Curie with λ-point.

title: One plasma clock
statement: Reflection skin-effect and plasma-frequency cutoff must share one ωp (or interband-shifted optical edge) class for a given metal.
notes: Al ~15 eV; Ag optical edge ~3.9 eV. If a later mapping needs a second independent clock for the same film this requirement goes to tension.

title: Underived penetration depth
statement: The screening buffer is located as δ = λ/4πk (optical) or √(2/ωμσ) (classical skin) or London λ. It is not yet derived from a more primitive node count.
notes: Same gap class on reflection skin and Meissner.

title: Coupled screening failure
statement: A film starved in connected thickness must lose ordinary reflectivity raise transmission toward and above the plasma edge and lose SPR in the same thickness window.
notes: Library already states the shared cliff on reflection plasma-cutoff and SPR.

title: Latch cell is the cliff
statement: The sharp hardware cliff of a latch is the grain / polar volume with KV (or the polar analog) above the thermal-escape line. The sample envelope is capacity not a second cliff.
notes: 25 kT is a timescale convention. Superparamagnetism owns the volume collapse.

title: Mesoscale coercivity
statement: Technical Hc is not Ha. Nucleation grain boundaries and dipolar coupling sit between the unit-cell barrier and the bulk force and are not yet a buffer/barrier spec.
notes: Reappears on hysteresis domains and the parent latch.

title: Polar depolarization buffer
statement: Ec and the depolarization field of a thin ferroelectric are mesoscale. The polar latch is located; the write-field spec is not.
notes: Electrical twin of mesoscale-coercivity.

title: Split R=0 from expulsion
statement: Zero resistance and complete field expulsion are related artifacts of one condensate with different failure envelopes. Type-II mixed state can hold R=0 after Meissner has failed.
notes: Split rule already in the library.

title: Pinning after Hc1
statement: Why R=0 survives between Hc1 and Hc2 is a pinning landscape. The design does not yet have a buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale step.
notes: Owned jointly by superconductivity and type-II entries.

title: Fluxoid increment 2e
statement: The measured increment in Φ0 = h/2e and in the Josephson lock is 2e. It is taken as data not derived from node rules.
notes: Located; origin of 2e vs e is a gap.

title: BEC is not this condensate
statement: A dilute alkali BEC has a thermal/density cliff and quantized winding but no measured pairing gap and is not held at zero continuous power. It must not be folded into gapped-condensate.
value_text: no pairing gap; not a latch
notes: Status tension records the family-fit problem the BEC entry already names.

title: No London λ
statement: Chargeless superflow has no electromagnetic screening length and no Meissner expulsion. Demanding λ of He-4 is a category error.
notes: Circulation quantum is h/m4 not h/2e.

title: Gapped name is loose
statement: He-4 collapse is loss of ρs at Tλ (and of superflow at vc) not a spectroscopic pairing gap. The family assignment is by critical-temperature protected mode not by a gap identification.
notes: Recorded on the He-4 entry.

title: Gate is single-particle
statement: One conversion event needs one node (electron atom shell). No collective buffer is required for the gate to open.
notes: Contrast with connected-spatial-buffer on screening.

title: Shared surface φ
statement: Photoelectric and thermionic conversion on the same surface must share one work-function class opened by hν or by heat.
notes: Do not identify φ with the optical plasma edge.

title: Shared crystal Eg
statement: Semiconductor gap absorption and photoconductivity in the same crystal must share one Eg read as opacity or as current.
notes: value_si is Si. Other crystals have their own Eg.

title: Underived gate energy
statement: φ Eg I shell binding energy and 2mec² are located as gates. Only pair production’s 2mec² is a rest-mass identity; the others are taken not derived from a surface-dipole or many-electron construction.
notes: Pair-production 1.022 MeV is the clean derived member of this family.

title: Pair needs a recoil partner
statement: Pair production above 1.022 MeV still fails without a nearby nucleus (or other momentum sink).
notes: Second hardware clause unique to this gate.

title: Finite mode count
statement: A grid of N ions has 3N mechanical modes and a spectral ceiling. There is no oscillator above ωD.
notes: Debye cutoff is the clock ceiling of the oscillator-grid.

title: Melting not derived
statement: Tm and the loss of Bragg / shear order are located. Lindemann is a criterion not a derivation of Tm from node rules.
notes: Grid-loss failure is real; the number is taken.

title: Underived grid couplings
statement: Moduli vs λs d_ij and α are taken as handbook couplings of the same grid. The grid and its collapses are located; the coupling magnitudes are not derived.
notes: Shared closure across elasticity magnetostriction piezoelectricity and thermal expansion.

title: No universal N
statement: The ensemble-average machine names a statistical buffer (1/√N Kn Fermi-slice) and does not attach a single node-count cliff analogous to a 10 nm film.
notes: This is the family-wide Medium mapping.

title: Defined constants are not extracted
statement: k and σ are defined SI constants. Treating them as QSA-extracted machine numbers over-claims.
notes: Recorded on the temperature blackbody and Stefan–Boltzmann entries.

title: Average replaced by order
statement: When a latch or a gap opens the original contributing population is no longer the one being averaged. Curie χ and γT must yield to the ordered or gapped output.
notes: Library already cross-cites magnet latch and superconductivity from the ensemble entries.

title: Nested pin is not the parent latch
statement: Exchange-bias collapse is TB of the AFM pin (TB ≤ TN) not the FM Curie point. Treating Hex as just another name for Ha hides the bilayer hardware.
notes: This is why exchange-pin is its own design.

title: Interface exchange underived
statement: Hex and TB/TN remain interface- and grain-level data. The two-latch topology is located; the interface Jex is not derived.
notes: Draft design; this closure is the reason it is not formal.
